steps.title: Import all required modules and APIs
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to enable component creation and state management for the regular expressions lesson.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to return a div element.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react' here

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App that returns a div element.
successCriteria: The App component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named App and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've named it App and it returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize state for input text
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable called 'text' with an empty string using useState.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into 'text' and 'setText'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'text' initialized to an empty string, ready to store user input.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into 'text' and 'setText'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state for the input text.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState correctly and destructuring the array into 'text' and 'setText'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for useState and ensure you're initializing 'text' with an empty string.

steps.title: Initialize state for regular expression pattern
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable named 'pattern' with an empty string as its initial value.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to create a state variable. The pattern will store the regular expression entered by the user.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a search query
const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'pattern' initialized to an empty string.
successCriteria: A state variable named 'pattern' is declared with useState and initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created state to store the regular expression pattern.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named 'pattern' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to initialize a state variable called 'pattern' with an empty string using useState.

steps.title: Initialize state for match results
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable called 'matches' with an empty array using useState.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after your existing state declarations. The initial value should be an empty array [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for an array
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a third state variable 'matches' initialized as an empty array, ready to store regular expression match results.
successCriteria: A state variable named 'matches' is declared with useState, initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to store match results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array initial value and naming the variable 'matches'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add a new useState call inside the component to create a 'matches' state variable initialized to [].

steps.title: Create a handler function to update text state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function called handleTextChange that takes an event parameter and updates the text state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the event object and calls setText with the value from the input event.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleTextChange function is defined inside the App component that will update the text state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The handleTextChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handleTextChange function that will update the text state when the user types in the input field.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and calls setText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleTextChange function isn't defined correctly. It should take an event parameter and update the text state with event.target.value.

steps.title: Create a handler function to update pattern state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function called handlePatternChange that takes an event object as a parameter and updates the 'pattern' state with the event's target value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an event parameter and calls setPattern with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handlePatternChange function that updates the pattern state when called with an event.
successCriteria: The handlePatternChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setPattern with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handlePatternChange function to update the pattern state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and calls setPattern with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should update the pattern state when called with an event.

steps.title: Create a handler function to execute regular expression matching
steps.instruction: Define a function called handleMatch inside your component that creates a RegExp object from the pattern state and executes the match() method on the text state, then updates the matches state with the results.
steps.hint: Use new RegExp() with the pattern state, then call .match() on the text state with that regex. Update the matches state with the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleMatch function is defined that uses the current pattern and text states to perform regex matching and updates the matches state.
successCriteria: The handleMatch function is defined, creates a RegExp from the pattern state, calls .match() on the text state, and updates the matches state with the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the regex matching handler. This function will be the core logic that connects your pattern and text inputs to produce match results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handleMatch function, but it's missing key parts. Make sure it creates a RegExp from the pattern state, calls .match() on the text state, and updates the matches state with the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleMatch function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create it inside your component, use new RegExp() with the pattern state, call .match() on the text state, and update the matches state.

steps.title: Add input elements and wire event handlers for text and pattern
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add two input elements: one for text input with value={text} and onChange={handleTextChange}, and another for pattern input with value={pattern} and onChange={handlePatternChange}.
steps.hint: Use <input> elements with type='text'. Connect the first input's value to the text state and its onChange to handleTextChange. Connect the second input's value to the pattern state and its onChange to handlePatternChange.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding controlled input elements
<input type='text' value={someState} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: Two text input fields appear in the UI: one for entering text to match against, and another for entering the regular expression pattern. Both inputs are controlled components that update their respective state values when typed into.
successCriteria: Two <input> elements are present in the return statement. The first input has value={text} and onChange={handleTextChange}. The second input has value={pattern} and onChange={handlePatternChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the two input fields and wired them to their respective state values and handlers. Now users can enter both text and pattern inputs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some input elements, but check that both inputs are present and properly connected. Make sure each input has both value and onChange attributes correctly set to their corresponding state and handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input elements are missing or not properly connected. Add two <input> elements with type='text' inside the return statement. Connect the first to text state and handleTextChange, and the second to pattern state and handlePatternChange.

steps.title: Add a match button and display results
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the return statement that calls handleMatch when clicked, and display the matches array results below the button.
steps.hint: Use the onClick event handler on a button element to trigger your handleMatch function, then show the matches state value in the UI.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have a button that triggers regular expression matching when clicked, and displays the match results below it.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick={handleMatch} is added, and the matches state is displayed in the UI.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the match button and results display. The button will trigger the regular expression matching function when clicked, and the results will be shown below.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure you have both: 1) a button with onClick={handleMatch}, and 2) display of the matches array results.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required elements are missing. Add a button that calls handleMatch when clicked, and display the matches array results below it.
